answer: Each identity borrows one book for a 70-credit bond plus a fee. Same-funding fees: first 26, k-th 26+6(k-1), 1000th 6020; 1000 fakes pay 3,023,000 plus 70,000 locked, no discount. Before the loan horizon ends, the borrower returns the book to the haven vault with a key-signed pulse tying its hash to its key. Any auditor recomputes the loan ledger against haven receipts; a missing book, reused hash, or foreign pulse burns the bond. A rented-book ring fails: the haven receipt names the original key, not the renter. An honest borrower pays 26 once and recovers the bond after return.
